(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;

(2) Guidance may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children.
(3) The form of participation shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 12

(1) The organization of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the UPTD-PPA.

(2) Provisions concerning UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

(3) In addition to establishing UPTD-PPA, to support the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. task force on violence against women and children; b. regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

NUMBER 6 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) Regional government establishes partnerships with the business world in organizing PPA.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through : a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women victims of violence; c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been removed from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 14

(1) The committee as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (3) letter b, consists of representatives from Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.

(2) Further provisions regarding the duties and functions of the committee are established by Regent's decision.

CHAPTER VIII

ASSISTANCE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Article 24

(1) The Regional Government may provide funding assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement PPA from acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

(2) Funding assistance, in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

NUMBER 6 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) Regional government establishes partnerships with the business world in organizing PPA.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through : a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women victims of violence; c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been removed from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 12

(1) The organization of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the UPTD-PPA.

(2) Provisions concerning UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

(3) In addition to establishing UPTD-PPA, to support the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. task force on violence against women and children; b. regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children.
(3) The form of participation shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 12

(1) The organization of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the UPTD-PPA.

(2) Provisions concerning UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

(3) In addition to establishing UPTD-PPA, to support the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. task force on violence against women and children; b. regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Article 9

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Article 12

(1) The organization of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the UPTD-PPA.

(2) Provisions concerning UPTD-PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated in a Regent Regulation.

(3) In addition to establishing UPTD-PPA, to support the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. task force on violence against women and children; b. regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children.
(3) The form of participation shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children.
(3) The form of participation shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection for women and children needs to be provided in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing PPA from acts of violence have not regulated protection measures in the Regions, so institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 8

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:

a. preventing acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth against women and children.
(3) The form of participation shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the regional head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPA, is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other issues. 8. Violence is any act against the law with or without the use of means against physical and psychological well-being that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the domestic sphere. 12. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 18. Mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity is an action or attitude that does not conform to applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms, encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or slavery-like practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim's body for profit, including but not limited to all prostitution and obscene activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that creates fear or restricts the inherent freedom of a person. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA, is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and advocacy, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking in the Regency of Pulang Pisau. 26.
